headline: Purchases and contracts for a $1,015,299 aircraft deicer and $611,533 Mount Hope Avenue sidewalk, plus a $3,048,959 WIC grant.
summary: Three purchases are up for committee approval, including a $116,889 carpet replacement and a $163,897.10 police data terminal purchase. Four items, including a $560,000 rock salt contract, go to the full Council with a committee recommendation.

TO:         Members of the Finance Committee 
FROM:  Lt. Jason Stuart, Bangor Police Department 
DATE:   September 9, 2026 
RE:  Sole-Source Procurement of Patrol PC RhinoTab M4 i7 Mobile Data Terminals 
  
Request 
The Bangor Police Department respectfully requests authorization to purchase 28 Patrol PC RhinoTab M4 i7 ruggedized 
tablets on a sole -source basis, rather than through a competitive request -for-bid process. The devices will replace the 
Department’s existing mobile data terminals (MDTs) installed in cruisers. 
 
Background 
In 2019, the Department selected Patrol PC’s first- generation Patrol PC RhinoTab as its standard MDT. Those units 
remain installed in all marked cruisers. Over the past seven years, the Department has had a consistently positive 
operational experience with Patrol PC hardware, docking, and support. 
 
City of Bangor Information Technology has advised the Department that Microsoft will soon discontinue support for 
the Windows version running on the current MDTs. Once that support ends, the existing devices will no longer be 
suitable for displaying or rec eiving Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) data, including criminal history, 
names, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, and other protected information. Replacement is required to maintain 
compliance and operational capability. The proposed RhinoTab M4 i7 units will be licensed and configured with 
Windows 11 and the security support necessary to continue displaying CJIS information. 
 
Evaluation of Alternatives 
Over the past several months, the Department tested and evaluated five models from four manufacturers: Panasonic, 
Getac, Dell, and Patrol PC. Each candidate device was field-tested in patrol operations. After each test period, officers 
were polled. Nearly unanimously, patrol officers selected the Patrol PC RhinoTab over the competing units. 
 
City IT staff have met with the Department on multiple occasions and have reviewed the specifications and operational 
requirements of the candidate tablets. The RhinoTab M4 i7 is t hree generations advanced from the hardware now in 
service, with modern components and current software support. It is purpose -built in Massachusetts specifically for 
first-responder use. 
 
Justification for Sole-Source Procurement 
Sole-source authorization is requested for the following independent and mutually reinforcing reasons: 
 
1. Operational preference and fitness for duty. After structured field testing against four manufacturers, officers selected 
the Patrol PC RhinoTab by a near -unanimous margin. Continuity of a platform already proven in Bangor cruisers 
reduces training and acclimation burdens. 
 
2. Compatibility with existing vehicle docks. Patrol PC tablets are backward-compatible with the docks already installed 
in Department cruisers. A change of manufacturer would require purchase and installation of new docks in every 
equipped vehicle.
2 
 
3. Documented cost avoidance. A local vehicle upfitter  quoted $29,939 to furnish and install docks for 28 MDTs. 
Remaining with Patrol PC avoids that cost in full, in addition to avoiding the vehicle downtime associated with dock 
replacement. 
 
 4. Continuity of a purpose-built first-responder platform. The RhinoTab is designed specifically for public-safety use. 
Combined with seven years of satisfactory service from the same vendor, this continuity supports reliability, parts 
familiarity, and support relationships already in place. 
 
Fiscal Summary 
If the Department were required to change manufacturers, dock hardware and installation alone would add $29,939, 
based on the quote from the local vendor for 28 units. That figure does not include additional staff time, vehicle 
downtime, or any difference in tablet unit price. Staying with Patrol PC eliminates the dock -and-installation line item 
because the Patrol PC fits the docks already in the cruisers. 
 
The total anticipated cost of this project, which includes the delivery of the MDT’s and supporting equipment and a 5-
year warranty, is $163,897.10. 
 
The Department has Capital Improvement Program funding to support this request.  
 
Recommendation 
The Department recommends that the Finance Committee authorize sole- source procurement of Patrol PC RhinoTab 
M4 i7 MDTs. City IT has reviewed the relevant specifications. Officer field evaluation, CJIS -driven obsolescence of 
the current fleet, Windows 11 I oT Enterprise licensing on the replacement units, and documented dock- compatibility 
savings together support this request. 
 
I am available to answer any questions you may have. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
  
Lieutenant Jason Stuart 
Bangor Police Department

OTHER COMMENTS:
Public Works joined with the City of Brewer to release an RFP for their annual road salt supply in 2027 .  The total 
volume of salt put out to bid was 10,200 tons with Bangor having the larger amount at 8,000 tons.  The bid was 
administered by David Cote, Public Works Director for the City of Brewer.  This is a coopertive purchase as defined 
under the procurement policy. 
Four bids ranged from $74.37/ton to $98.44/ton, delivered.  Current State of Maine salt bids are coming in at $74 
and higher, and include a requirement for price increases in the event of tariffs, as salt is generally imported from 
Canada and Chile. 
Staff recommends award of the FY27 rock salt bid to New England Salt Co. for $74.37/ton, delivered. Funding for 
road salt purchases are included in the proposed FY27 Public Works Operational budget which equals 7,530 tons.

Authorizing the City Manager to Accept and Appropriate $841,177 in Administrative Funds and $2,207,782 in 
Food Dollar Pass-Through Funds, for a Total of $3,048,959 in Grant Funding from the Maine Department of 
Health and Human Services for the Women, Infants, and Children Program 
This Resolve will authorize the City Manager to accept and appropriate a total of $3,048,959 in grant 
funds for the Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) Program for a coverage period of October 1, 2026 
through September 30, 2027. 
Public Health and Community Services, WIC Nutrition Program currently services a monthly average 
of 2,700 participants and has been operating the program since 1974.  The proposed agreement 
provides $841,177 in administrative funding for WIC, Breastfeeding Peer Counseling (BFPC), and 
Farmers Market Nutrition Program (FMNP) services and $2,207,782 for food dollar costs, for a total 
of $3,048,959.
